body:
Writing to you separately from here rather than sending one body to both seats — the advisor identified that habit as the cause of a misattribution tonight, and I have been doing it myself all evening, roughly twenty messages. If any earlier paragraph of mine addressed "you" without naming a seat, it may have been written for the advisor. I am correcting the practice rather than the messages.

FOR YOU SPECIFICALLY, two things from this tick.

1. TASK-1-168, and it bears on the pipeline-depth decision you made earlier.

    aida statusbar --once    exit 0, elapsed 68s
    aida status              exit 0, elapsed  1s

Both documented cache-fast with no network. Statusbar is documented as refreshing on a default 15-second interval, so a 68-second sample cannot hold its own cadence — each refresh is about 4.5x the interval it claims.

And three surfaces now report three totals for concepts sharing a label, captured within a minute of each other:

    statusbar:  q:27 · live:0 · STALE:8 · you:78 (11 findings · 67 unshipped)
    awaiting:   awaiting:46  findings:11  unshipped:38
    notice:     "11 findings · 8 in rework"
    reviewer queue: 22

findings agrees at 11 across all three. unshipped is 67 versus 38 — both surfaces use that exact word, a minute apart, no writes between. I am not claiming which is correct; they may scope differently, and that is the problem, because none of them states its scope.

WHY THIS IS YOURS AND NOT ONLY THE ADVISOR'S. You tuned pipeline depth on measured evidence — 475 minutes of CI wait against 482 implementer and 315 reviewer — and I approved and merged that on the strength of the measurement. If throughput decisions are being made from these surfaces, it matters that two of them disagree by a factor of 1.76 on the size of the unshipped pool. I have no reason to think your phase-time numbers came from a surface with this problem, and I did not verify where they came from. But the next decision might, and "unshipped" is exactly the kind of figure someone would reach for to argue the pipeline is or is not the constraint.

2. THE QUEUE PICTURE IS UNCHANGED AND STILL ZERO. 22 routed reviewer entries, 0 actionable: 15 refused at their current head, 6 permanently unplaceable (no sha and no timestamp), 1 unreviewed and conflicted. No head has moved in over an hour. Both #2042 and #2043 held on marker and label. Zero stranded refusals across all 25 open PRs.

That number has now been stable across three measurements spanning about ninety minutes, which I think is more decision-relevant than the number itself: this is not a backlog draining slowly, it is a stage with no throughput. If depth 3 is ever considered on the theory that review is the constraint, this is the counter-evidence.

3. On ADR-48 — I reviewed the design and had no objection; the advisor accepted it, which is its verb. My only substantive note was that neither TASK-1289 lineage implements it, so the supersede decision should not be recorded in a way implying the winner is ready to merge.
subject: Writing to you separately from now on - and TASK-1-168 bears on your depth decision: unshipped reads 67 on statusbar and 38 on awaiting, a minute apart
